record.Full citation: Dörfel, Leoni, and Rieke Ammoneit. 2026. Evaluation of Inductive Coding with LLMs. Education Sciences 16(8): 1314. https://doi.org/10.3390/educsci16081314.
record.Title: Evaluation of Inductive Coding with LLMs
record.Publication history notes: Received 14 July 2026; revised 7 August 2026; accepted 13 August 2026; published 17 August 2026. Version of record was available before the 24 August 2026 review cutoff.
record.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: 0 citations in the Crossref is-referenced-by-count field, retrieved 2026-08-24
record.Relationship/dependence family: Dörfel geography-education stereotyping interview family — reanalyzes part of the interview dataset and the human qualitative-content-analysis code system reported by Dörfel, Ammoneit, and Peter (2025a, 2025b); it is not an independent-corpus replication.
record.Research objective: Develop an iterative prompting framework for ChatGPT code-system induction and transcript coding, then compare its structural, semantic, and coding-unit outputs with a prior human qualitative content analysis of the same 11 interviews. The three comparison questions ask whether the code systems can be mapped semantically, whether mapped codes refer to the same coding units, and whether the systems differ structurally.
record.Claimed qualitative methodology: Kuckartz and Rädiker seven-step qualitative content analysis for the human analysis, alongside an iterative ChatGPT framework described as inductive coding and grounded in Kuckartz-style qualitative content analysis.
record.Actual operationalized methodology: Hybrid two-branch comparison. The human branch identifies 86 coding units, applies three deductive main codes, inductively derives 20 subcodes, revises the structure, and recodes all material. The ChatGPT branch induces one code system per transcript, synthesizes the 11 systems five times in separate sessions, retains cross-run codes appearing in at least three systems, and then applies the finalized 14-subcode codebook deductively to each transcript five times, retaining assignments appearing in at least three runs. SBERT/Hungarian mapping, coding-unit Jaccard, network analysis with null models, and an author qualitative comparison evaluate the two outputs.
record.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: hybrid — human analysis uses deductive main codes plus inductive subcodes; ChatGPT first induces and consolidates a codebook, then deductively applies that fixed codebook
record.Domain: German geography education; teacher accounts of stereotyping in geography classrooms
record.Dataset name: Part of the Dörfel et al. (2025b) stereotyping-in-geography-classes interview dataset: 11 anonymous semi-structured online interviews with German geography teachers
record.Public or restricted data: mixed — the Zenodo deposit is open and provides coding matrices, code systems, analysis scripts, and intermediate results; the original interview transcripts are not present in the inspected public file inventory, and their access status is not reported
record.Number of participants: 11 German geography teachers: 9 in-service and 2 pre-service
record.Approximate corpus size: 11 transcripts containing 86 coding units identified for the human content analysis; word and token counts are not reported
record.Language: German for transcripts, prompting, coding, code systems, and quantitative analyses; the final code system was translated into English with DeepL on 8 June 2026 for presentation only
record.Sensitive-data status: potentially sensitive education-interview material about stereotyping; authors state that transcripts were fully anonymized, contained no identifying information, and could not be re-identified
record.Model family: OpenAI ChatGPT/GPT-5.2; Sentence-BERT used for downstream semantic comparison
record.Prompting strategy: Role-, instruction-, and context-based prompts condition the model on the research questions and one complete transcript at a time. The workflow generates 11 transcript-level codebooks, iteratively merges them, repeats synthesis in five separate project chats with memory off, consolidates codes present in at least three of five systems, and applies a fixed codebook with coding-unit IDs, verbatim passages, definition-referenced justifications, and allowance for multiple or no codes. Complete prompts are reproduced in Appendix A, Figures A1-A4.
record.Single-agent or multi-agent: single-model or non-agent pipeline — independent ChatGPT sessions and repeated calls are aggregated, but no interacting multi-agent architecture is used
record.Agent roles: ChatGPT is prompted as an experienced qualitative educational researcher/research assistant; no differentiated multi-agent roles are used
record.Human role: Researchers formulate the research questions and prompts, refine the initial prompt after unwanted definitional codes, supply transcripts/codebooks, conduct or reuse the prior human qualitative content analysis, qualitatively interpret the comparison, and report that all AI outputs were critically reviewed, validated, and interpreted by the authors.
record.Unit of analysis: One full interview transcript for initial codebook induction; labeled coding units and their verbatim coded passages for final code assignment; code pairs and coding-unit-by-code matrices for the quantitative comparison
record.Generated outputs: Eleven transcript-level code systems; five independently synthesized systems; one final three-main-code/14-subcode ChatGPT codebook; five coding outputs per transcript with majority-retained assignments; semantic mappings, Jaccard results, code co-occurrence networks, and a qualitative comparison
record.Evidence/provenance mechanism: The synthesis prompt requires source-code identifiers and documentation of merge decisions. The final coding prompt requires a labeled coding unit, the complete coded passage, the assigned code, and a definition-referenced justification. The public deposit supplies both code systems, coding matrices, scripts, and intermediate mappings, but not the original transcripts or complete ChatGPT session logs.
record.Baselines: A prior human qualitative content analysis of the same material, organized around three main codes and 20 inductively derived subcodes across 86 coding units; it predates the ChatGPT comparison but shares authors and is not an independent multi-analyst reference standard
record.Number of runs or seeds: Initial code induction once for each of 11 transcripts; five synthesis runs in separate project-chat sessions with memory off; one final cross-synthesis consolidation; and five independent coding runs for each of 11 transcripts (55 transcript-coding runs). Random seeds, temperature, and other sampling settings are not reported.
record.Automatic metrics: SBERT cosine similarity on concatenated code labels and definitions; globally optimized one-to-one Hungarian matching with a 0.60 retention threshold; code-pair and global Jaccard indices; run-to-run Jaccard; network density, global clustering coefficient, and eigenvector centrality; 10,000 Curveball null-model randomizations with z-scores, 95% null intervals, and two-sided Monte Carlo p-values
record.Human-evaluation design: The authors qualitatively compare the two code systems along structural composition/cross-method convergence, granularity/contextualization, and explanatory logic/agency, in addition to using the prior human content analysis as the comparator. No independent, blinded evaluation of coding quality is reported.
record.Number and expertise of evaluators: The number, expertise, and independence of the human content analyst(s) and qualitative comparison evaluator(s) are not reported in this article; both authors are affiliated with an institute for geography education.
record.Inter-rater reliability: No human-human inter-rater reliability is reported. ChatGPT repeat-run stability is reported instead: overall Jaccard 0.83 across five runs per transcript, with transcript-level values from 0.66 to 0.91.
record.Statistical analysis: Cosine-similarity matrix and 0.60 threshold; Hungarian global one-to-one optimization; global and pairwise Jaccard indices; descriptive network comparison; and separate 10,000-randomization Curveball null models for each code network, yielding z-scores, 95% null intervals, and two-sided Monte Carlo p-values. No multiplicity adjustment is reported.
record.Principal results: The final ChatGPT system had three main codes and 14 subcodes versus three main codes and 20 subcodes in the human analysis. Sixty-three code pairs had cosine similarity at least 0.60; 13 of 14 optimized pairs met the threshold, with retained similarities from 0.60 to 0.81. Coding-unit overlap was much lower: global Jaccard 0.39, pairwise range 0-0.86, five pairs above 0.60, and five below 0.14. ChatGPT repeat-run Jaccard was 0.83 overall. Human/ChatGPT network density was 0.40/0.36 and clustering 0.56/0.61; neither network differed significantly from its own null model. The qualitative comparison found broader ChatGPT codes, six missing human subcodes, omitted actor- and geography-specific distinctions, and concentration around fewer central categories.
record.Ethics and privacy treatment: Authors report fully anonymized prior interview transcripts, no identifying information or re-identification possibility, and informed consent from the original interviewees. They state that the secondary analysis did not involve human subjects and therefore did not require a new institutional review. AI use is disclosed, but data-processing terms, transmission safeguards, and the ChatGPT deployment's retention/training settings are not reported.
record.Reproducibility resources: Appendix A reproduces all four prompt formats. The model snapshot and memory setting are reported. Open Zenodo dataset version 1.0 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21108082) supplies R scripts for SBERT/Hungarian mapping, Jaccard, and network analysis; both code systems; both coding matrices; and intermediate similarity/mapping/Jaccard outputs. Original transcripts, full model outputs/session logs, random seeds, temperature, and complete runtime/package versions are not supplied or not reported.
record.Author-reported limitations: Small, topic-specific dataset; limited generalizability; prompt sensitivity despite refinement and repeated runs; alternative mapping strategies could change correspondences; qualitative content analysis is interpretive and multiple valid code systems can arise; the comparison is between two interpretations rather than against an objective standard. The discussion also identifies the model's black-box process and limited domain-specific contextualization.
record.Additional validity concerns: Reviewer-identified: the human comparator is a single prior code-system family with overlapping authors, not an independent consensus or quality gold standard. Prompt refinement on this same corpus/RQs and three-of-five majority filtering can favor stable, broad categories and suppress minority codes; the reported 0.83 repeatability therefore does not establish coding quality or interpretive validity. The 0.60 SBERT threshold is not empirically validated here, Hungarian matching forces exclusivity, and the global coding-unit Jaccard of 0.39 demonstrates that label similarity is not evidence of shared interpretation. Missing transcripts, session logs, sampling settings, and independent human quality judgments limit auditability; cloud-model data governance is also underreported.
record.Relationship to prior papers: Reuses part of Dörfel, Ammoneit, and Peter's 2025 geography-teacher interview corpus and their published human qualitative content analysis/code system; the 2026 Zenodo deposit contains the current paper's derived code systems, matrices, scripts, and intermediate outputs.
record.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Direct core evidence that semantic code-label agreement and within-model stability can coexist with low source-unit overlap and lost domain-specific distinctions. It motivates source-grounded evaluation, independent quality assessment, plurality/minority-code preservation, prompt-development separation from evaluation, and reporting that distinguishes repeatability from qualitative validity.

quality_score.Title: Evaluation of Inductive Coding with LLMs

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: Adequate: §2.1 (pp.3-4) names Kuckartz and Rädiker's procedure and reports coding units, deductive main codes, inductive subcodes, revision/recoding, analytical use, and software; §§2.2.1-2.2.5 (pp.4-5) separately specify the LLM operations.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Partial: the 11 interviews and 86 coding units are relevant, interpretively demanding, and held constant across methods (§2, p.3), but the single small topic-specific corpus constrains the broader workflow claims (§4.4, p.19).

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Adequate: §§2.2-2.3 (pp.4-8), Appendix A (pp.21-25), and the linked Zenodo scripts document the model snapshot, prompting phases, session separation/memory setting, thresholds, embedding model, mapping, Jaccard, and network/null-model procedures.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: Partial: the comparator is a temporally prior human qualitative content analysis of exactly the same data (§§2-2.1, pp.3-4), but it shares authors, represents one valid interpretation rather than an objective standard, and lacks an independent multi-analyst quality reference (§4.4, p.19).

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Partial: §2.3.5 and §3.5 (pp.8, 15-16) add qualitative comparison across three relevant dimensions, but evaluator number, expertise, independence, blindness, decision protocol, and reliability are not reported.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Partial: SBERT/Hungarian, Jaccard, and network/null-model measures triangulate label, assignment, and structural similarity (§§2.3.1-2.3.4, pp.6-8), but the 0.60 threshold is not validated for qualitative equivalence, exclusive matching can create questionable pairs, and global Jaccard 0.39 shows semantic similarity is not coding validity (§§3.2-3.3, pp.10-13).

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Partial: §4.4 (p.19) explicitly states that multiple valid coding systems may arise and rejects an objective-gold interpretation, but the design evaluates one human system and three-of-five aggregation suppresses alternative/minority LLM interpretations (§2.2.4-2.2.5, p.5).

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Partial: the prompts require source-code identifiers, merge documentation, verbatim passages, coding-unit IDs, and definition-referenced justifications (Table 2, p.4; Table 3, p.5; Appendix A.2/A.4, pp.23-25), but transcripts and complete run logs are not in the public deposit.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Adequate: synthesis is repeated five times in separate sessions with memory off and each of 11 transcripts is coded five times; Table 5 (p.10) reports per-transcript and overall run-to-run Jaccard, with an explicit three-of-five retention rule (§§2.2.3-2.2.5, p.5).

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: Partial: p.21 reports anonymization, consent, the secondary-analysis IRB rationale, and AI use, but does not report the ChatGPT deployment's data transmission, retention, training-exclusion, contractual, or governance safeguards.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Partial: Appendix A (pp.21-25), the exact ChatGPT snapshot (§2.2, p.4), and open Zenodo code systems, matrices, scripts, and intermediate outputs support reproduction; original transcripts, complete model outputs/session logs, sampling settings, and full runtime versions are unavailable or unreported.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: Partial: the discussion and limitations appropriately emphasize one corpus, plurality, prompt/mapping sensitivity, and weak domain-specific differentiation (§§4.1-4.4, pp.16-19), but Key Learning I calls repeated-output agreement 'methodological robustness' (p.20), which is stronger than repeatability and is not supported as coding quality by global human overlap J=0.39.

quality_score.Interpretation caution: The total is a compact audit aid, not a ranking of study quality; dimensions must be interpreted individually against the paper's stated claim.
